MAKING A STATEMENT
Tuesday 22 April 2014: “Manchester United has announced that David Moyes has left the club. The club would like to place on record its thanks for the hard work, honesty and integrity he brought to the role.”
Monday 23 May 2016: “Louis van Gaal is to leave Manchester United, with immediate effect. Executive vice chairman Ed Woodward said: ‘I would like to thank Louis and his staff for their excellent work in the past two years culminating in winning a record-equalling 12th FA Cup for the club (and securing him a title in four different countries). He has behaved with great professionalism and dignity throughout his time here.’ A decision on a successor as manager will be announced soon.”
Tuesday 18 December 2018: “Manchester United announces that manager José Mourinho has left the club with immediate effect. The club would like to thank José for his work during his time at Manchester United and to wish him success in the future. A new caretaker manager will be appointed until the end of the current season, while the club conducts a thorough recruitment process for a new, full-time manager.”
Sunday 21 November 2021: “Manchester United announces that Ole Gunnar Solskjær has left his role as manager. Ole will always be a legend at Manchester United and it is with regret that we have reached this difficult decision. While the past few weeks have been disappointing, they should not obscure all the work he has done over the past three years to rebuild the foundations for long-term success.”
Monday 28 October 2024: “Erik ten Hag has left his role as Manchester United men’s first-team manager. Erik was appointed in April 2022 and led the club to two domestic trophies, winning the Carabao Cup in 2023 and the FA Cup in 2024. We are grateful to Erik for everything he has done during his time with us and wish him well for the future.”
Monday 5 January 2026: “Ruben Amorim has departed his role as head coach of Manchester United. Ruben was appointed in November 2024 and led the team to a Uefa Europa League final in Bilbao in May. With Manchester United sitting sixth in the Premier League, the club’s leadership has reluctantly made the decision that it is the right time to make a change. This will give the team the best opportunity of the highest possible Premier League finish. The club would like to thank Ruben for his contribution to the club and wishes him well for the future.”
Thursday 12 November 2026: “Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach. After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions. Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.”
LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE
Join Simon Burnton for piping hot MBM coverage of Barcelona 2-0 Arsenal in the Women’s Champions League from 5.45pm (all times GMT). Then join Scott Murray for Harry Kane’s coronation as England’s record cap winner, and England 4-1 Croatia in the Nations League from 8pm.
QUOTE OF THE DAY
“First of all we would like to sincerely apologise to the Korean public and football fans for the concern caused by recent reports concerning the national team. At our recent meeting we gathered to share our thoughts on the national team openly and honestly. By listening directly to one another and discussing matters we had not had sufficient opportunities to address, we were able to gain a better understanding of each other’s positions” – the Korean FA and players Son Heung-min Kim Min-jae, Lee Jae-sung, Hwang In-beom and Hwang Hee-chan issue a finely worded non-apology for what definitely was not a massive falling out between squad members after their early exit from the World Cup.
FOOTBALL DAILY LETTERS
 Oh no! Where will the USA! USA! USA! ever be able to find a manager who could lead us to the dizzying heights of yet another humiliating defeat in the round of 16? A completely empty safari shirt on a clothes hanger could do that. Now he’s leaving the national team to prioritise a club team, which is exactly what he criticised Christian Pulisic for doing a while back. A $10m dollar buyout from Manchester United is a way more appealing prospect than another World Cup cycle with this guy. Adios, Mauricio. I’d add gracias, but for what, exactly?” – Chi.
 If any Manchester United fans weren’t already feeling that their board had totally lost its moral compass, then might I suggest that in holding the board meeting to seal Michael Carrick’s fate in Monaco a new bar in tone-deafness has been set. Out of touch, no? Pas du tout. Bonne chance, Mauricio, you are going to need it fella. Meanwhile, let’s pencil in the next board meeting for six months’ time or so. Circus Circus in Las Vegas anyone? Might be too many clowns” – John Collins.
 With Lil Wayne doing his bit in the jungle, how long before we do actually see Don Pochettino playing a starring role in the Joel & Jim-hosted caper show I’m A Previously Respectable Manager … Get Me Out Of Here?” – Ken Muir.
If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Chi. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

מנצ'סטר יונייטד מחזיקה במסורת של פרסום הודעות פרידה רשמיות ומכובדות למאמנים המסיימים את תפקידם במועדון. לאורך השנים, המועדון פרסם הודעות תודה דומות עבור שורה ארוכה של מאמנים מרכזיים שעמדו על הקווים.

בין השמות הבולטים שזכו להודעות פרידה רשמיות דומות ניתן למצוא את דייוויד מויס, לואי ואן חאל, ז'וזה מוריניו, אולה גונאר סולשקאר, אריק טן האח, רובן אמורים ומיכאל קאריק. הודעות אלו כוללות בדרך כלל הבעת תודה על העבודה הקשה והמקצועיות שהפגינו בתפקידם, גם כאשר תוצאות הקבוצה הובילו לפרידה.
